bib.title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Large Language Models with Zero-initialized Attention

question: Can LLaMA be turned into an instruction-following (and multi-modal) model by training only a tiny set of prefix prompts, without destabilising the frozen model?
hypothesis: Randomly initialised adaption prompts disturb the pre-trained model early in training; a zero-initialised gate lets instruction signal be injected progressively, giving stability and better final performance.
contributions: LLaMA-Adapter: 1.2M learnable parameters on frozen LLaMA 7B, under one hour on 8 A100 GPUs
Zero-initialized attention with learnable zero gating
Zero-init attention generalises to ViT, RoBERTa, CLIP fine-tuning

method.summary: Learnable prompts of length K are prefixed to word tokens in the top L layers of a frozen LLaMA; attention scores of the prompt part get a separate softmax multiplied by tanh(g_l), g_l initialised at zero and learned per head. For images, a frozen CLIP encoder feature is projected and added element-wise to the prompts.
method.task: parameter-efficient instruction tuning and visual instruction tuning

datasets.name: Alpaca self-instruct data
datasets.source: Taori et al. 2023 (GPT-3.5 expanded from 175 seeds)

datasets.name: ScienceQA
datasets.split: multi-modal train set for tuning, in-domain test; ablations on validation
datasets.preprocessing: question, textual context and options concatenated in one sentence

datasets.name: Open LLM benchmark (ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA)
Base-to-novel (ImageNet, Caltech101, Flowers102)
datasets.split: train on base classes few-shot, test base and novel

models.name: LLaMA-Adapter
models.params: 1.2M tuned (1.8M with visual projection; Table 4 reports 1.79 at L=30)
models.architecture: prefix adaption prompts K=10 in last L=30 layers with zero-init gated attention

other.gate: tanh(g_l), g_l zero-init, one per head

models.name: CLIP image encoder
models.architecture: CLIP, multi-scale global features, bottleneck MLP projection (0.6M)

training.objective: inferred: next-token language modelling loss on instruction responses (not stated)
training.wall_clock: less than one hour (Alpaca 3 hours, Alpaca-LoRA 1.5 hours)

other.stage2: freeze projection, tune zero-init attention on Alpaca + LLaVA-I
other.scienceqa: freeze image encoder and LLaMA; train projection and zero-init attention

inference.prompting: ScienceQA: question, textual context, options concatenated sequentially

metrics.name: GPT-4 win count
metrics.definition: GPT-4 compares two responses on 80 questions

eval.protocol: single run per setting reported; no seeds, no significance tests stated

availability.weights: released per abstract ('Code and models are released')

evidence.quote: The warmup epochs, batch size, learning rate, and weight decay are set to 2, 64, 0.009, and 0.02, respectively.

results.claim: Zero-initialized attention raises ScienceQA validation accuracy by 43.08 points over random init of the same adapter.
results.setup: LLaMA-7B + adapter (K=10, L=30), ScienceQA val, multi-modal model
results.quote: it contributes to a significant +43.08% gain on ScienceQA’s validation set

results.claim: Randomly initialised adapter reaches 40.77% on ScienceQA val, about Random Choice (39.83).
results.setup: Same as above, random init of prompts and gate
results.quote: the randomly initialized baseline only achieves 40.77% accuracy

results.claim: Multi-modal LLaMA-Adapter scores 85.19 average on ScienceQA test, above GPT-4 CoT 83.99 and MM-CoT 84.91.
results.setup: ScienceQA test, fine-tuned on ScienceQA train, 1.8M tuned params

results.claim: Text-only LLaMA-Adapter_T scores 78.31 on ScienceQA; adding visual condition gives +6.88.
Adapter tunes 1.2M parameters and trains in 1 hour on 8 A100, vs Alpaca 7B in 3 hours and Alpaca-LoRA 4.2M in 1.5 hours.
results.table: Table 1, row LLaMA-Adapter, column Training Time

results.claim: Layer count ablation: 30 inserted layers gives 83.85 val acc, better than 32 (81.03) and 10 (55.95).
results.setup: ScienceQA val, last L layers of LLaMA-7B

results.claim: Open LLM benchmark average: LLaMA-Adapter 52.2 vs Alpaca 49.23 and Alpaca-LoRA 50.73.
results.setup: ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA; 7B models trained on 52K Alpaca data
results.note: LLaMA-Adapter is below Alpaca-LoRA on MMLU (34.9 vs 37.1).

results.claim: MME perception score 973 for LLaMA-Adapter vs LLaVA 503 and MiniGPT-4 867.
results.table: Table 3, row LLaMA-Adapter, column MME P

results.claim: Alpaca-LoRA at ranks 2/4/8/16 averages 50.9/50.8/50.7/50.8 on Open LLM, all below LLaMA-Adapter 52.2.
Zero-init attention on ViT-B/16 VTAB-1k: Natural 81.74, Specialized 84.43, Structured 56.75 vs VPT 78.48 / 82.43 / 54.98.
results.setup: ViT-B/16 pre-trained on ImageNet-21k, VTAB-1k 19 tasks

results.claim: On SQuAD 2.0 RoBERTa-large, zero-init gets F1 87.2 vs P-tuning v2 85.5 and full 89.4.
results.table: Table 7, row Zero-init., column SQuAD 2.0 F1

results.claim: With 204K VQAv2 added, MME total rises from 1222 to 1618.
results.setup: Instruction tuning with Alpaca + LLaVA-I + VQAv2 (204K)

results.claim: GPT-4 judged benchmark: LLaMA-Adapter wins 82 vs Alpaca and 90 vs Alpaca-LoRA in the figure labels (numbers extracted from Fig 5 without labels).
results.setup: 80 questions, GPT-4 as judge (Chiang et al. 2023)
results.note: Counts not tied to labels in the text; the text only says 'more win'

limits: No seeds, variances or significance tests reported.
Instruction-following quality judged by GPT-4 on only 80 questions; win counts given only in Fig 5 without a text table.
Optimizer, LR schedule, sequence length, precision not stated.
Zero-init ablation done on multi-modal ScienceQA val, not on language instruction following.
Table 4 shows inserting into all 32 layers is worse than 30 (81.03 vs 83.85), but text also says 'simply inserting into all layers is generally a good solution'.
Lower MMLU than Alpaca-LoRA in Table 18 (34.9 vs 37.1).

terms.definition: learnable gating factor, initialised at zero, that scales the softmaxed attention scores of the adaption prompts

concurrent multi-modal LLM; LLaVA-I data used
